evidence: The Ru film thickness and mass density were extracted from a Philips X’Pert MPD x-ray reflectometer (XRR) and the crystal structure from a grazing incidence x-ray diffractometer (GI-XRD). Rutherford backscattering spectroscopy (RBS) using a 2 MeV 2He+ beam at the singletron facility of the Eindhoven University of Technology was employed to measure the areal densities of the Ru films. The sheet resistance of the Ru films was measured at room temperature by a four-point probe (FPP). Time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) was performed by a dual beam ION-TOF IV instrument. The roughness of the Ru films was investigated by atomic force microscopy (AFM) using a Veeco Dimension 3100 scanning probe microscope. The nucleation of the Ru films on TiN was studied by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) using the FEI Tecnai F30ST microscope. The presence of O in the films was examined by ToF-SIMS. XPS results on the thermal ALD film corroborated that the Ru was in the metallic state. The XRD spectra only revealed crystalline peaks related to Ru and no peaks from RuO2 could be identified. The surface roughness of the films was investigated by AFM. The results from the TEM measurements on the TiN-covered membranes are shown.
